hypothesis: Candidate V1's ranking mechanism was correctly implemented but diluted because only 92 of 270 Train rows contain SELECTED-to-PLAUSIBLE pairs. Increasing only lambdaRank by the exact fixed dilution compensator should make the preference gradient comparable to BCE without adding absolute positive pressure to plausible labels, improving P0 ordering and reducing plausible false positives.
exactChangeFromV1: lambdaRank only: 1/18 -> (270/92)*(1/18) = 15/92. No other code, data, model, optimization, inference, threshold, or selection change.
finalPolicy: No Final Test file reads, inference, error inspection, tuning, or model-selection use.

training.checkpointRule: save and evaluate the final one-epoch checkpoint only

loss.bceReduction: mean over unmasked Product-18 cells within each row
loss.ranking: mean softplus(z_plausible - z_selected) over the within-row Cartesian product
loss.rowReduction: L_bce + lambdaRank * L_rank, then unweighted batch mean

stoppingAndSelectionRule: one epoch; final checkpoint only; KEEP_CANDIDATE only on all nine unchanged Dev gates, otherwise REJECT_CANDIDATE; no restart or rescue run

expectedMeasurableP0Effect.directionalSelectionMacro: greater than V1 0.445437; unchanged gate requires at least incumbent 0.470238 + 0.080
expectedMeasurableP0Effect.rawRankingMacro: greater than V1 0.535714; unchanged gate requires at least incumbent 0.552579 + 0.050
expectedMeasurableP0Effect.pairGuard: at least five of seven pairs improve strictly vs incumbent and no pair regresses more than 0.050
